title: Bounded arithmetic negative translation and universal conservation

based_on.title: From Constructive Mathematics to Computable Analysis via the Realizability Interpretation (doctoral thesis)
based_on.pages: §1.3.2 printed p.25, HA definition only; elementary internal developments supplied locally

summary: Convert expanded bounded formulas to and from their fixed negative translations, then obtain PA-to-HA conservation under a finite universal prefix.
abstract: A bounded arithmetic assertion may contain finite searches whose limits remain variables. Its expansion therefore contains genuine quantifiers, even when it abbreviates a simple order comparison. We show that Heyting arithmetic proves each expanded bounded assertion equivalent to its fixed negative translation. The proof retains the actual order guards and witnesses and uses internal decision proofs to remove double negation at bounded searches. Adding any finite universal prefix then gives a conservation theorem: every Peano arithmetic proof of such a sentence yields a Heyting arithmetic proof of the original sentence. An unbounded existential needs a further argument.
